core_obligations: Part (1) for sheaves of sets (proof lines 8266-8278): the author computes the stalk of f_*F at a geometric point as the product of the stalks of F over the finitely many geometric points of the fibre.
Part (1) for abelian sheaves (proof lines 8278-8284): in the abelian case the same computation gives a direct sum, because finite products and finite direct sums of abelian groups agree.

Part (2) (proof lines 8284-8289): the vanishing of the higher direct images follows from the description of the stalks together with the fact that the higher cohomology of a sheaf on the spectrum of a strictly henselian local ring in the relevant degrees is carried by the finite fibre.
proof_roadmap: Compute the stalk of the pushforward as a product over the finite fibre.
Observe that for abelian sheaves this product is a direct sum.
Deduce the vanishing of the higher direct images.
difficulty_reason: The proposition computes the stalks of the pushforward along a finite morphism, as a product over the finitely many points of the fibre for sheaves of sets and as a direct sum for abelian sheaves, and deduces the vanishing of the higher direct images (statement lines 8244-8264). The proof computes the stalk in both settings (proof lines 8266-8284) and then derives the vanishing in positive degrees from the same description of the stalks (proof lines 8284-8289). The non-formal content is the use of finiteness of the fibre and the identification of the product with the direct sum in the abelian case. The claim is H2: two computations and one vanishing, all written out.
